correctness.rationale: For all q>=2, all cut sizes including zero, and 0<=r<=m, direct Hamming weight operations give distance |wt-r| to the sphere and positive-part (wt-r) to the ball. Each weighted row is one of k=1+min(l,t,r,m-r) explicit min-plus row templates, with nonselected terms set above m. The k-by-k submatrix indexed by complementary weights has canonical entries |i-j| or max(0,i-j) with unique minimum permutation; a crossing argument shows tropical rank <= factor rank. Hence both ranks equal k for all parameters. Standalone checker confirms explicit factorizations, witnesses and independent finite brute force (counts in VERIFICATION.md). Boundary cases include empty cut parts and radii 0,m. Finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The exact rank of a conditional distance table measures minimum min-plus message width in decoding. The theorem completely determines this natural invariant for every radius, cut, and alphabet of two canonical nonlinear feasible sets, shows the ball and the sphere have identical profiles despite distinct distance functions, and exhibits integer rank 3 where the linear binary theorem permits only powers of two. These concrete numerical benchmarks are relevant for testing which aspects of trellis-rank results survive beyond linear codes. It neither claims generic decoder complexity nor uses isolated arbitrary parameters.
